tables.heading_context: ## 1. Models of Disability — The Model Decides What You Build
rows: disability is someone else's (clinical) problem; nothing to design
the *environment/interface* is the problem to change
interaction of body, activity, participation, context
function is contextual; measure participation, not just impairment
redesign the environment to fit more people
reframes disability as a *design* variable you control

tables.heading_context: ## 3. How Assistive Technology Interacts — The Accessibility Tree
rows: what kind of control? (button, link, checkbox)
`<div onclick>` → no role → invisible to AT
custom slider with no exposed value
menu that looks open but reports collapsed
error/help text not tied to its field
radio group with no group; header not tied to cell
ask **for whom, doing what, with which AT**
accessibility is a per-user, per-task capability, not a global flag (Big Picture, §2)
use the **native element** first; add ARIA only to fill gaps

no ARIA is better than bad ARIA; native semantics give **role/state behavior + keyboard** for free, but you still supply the accessible **name** where needed (icon buttons, inputs), **value/state only when applicable**, and **relationships/descriptions** where required (§3)
verify **name + role** (value/state when applicable; + description/relationships) and keyboard operability
AT reads the a11y tree; keyboard, touch/pointer/voice/switch are distinct mechanisms (§3)
treat as **low recall** (a minority of barriers; §6); run manual audit + AT walkthrough + user test
conformance is a scaffold, not usability (§6, §7)
it means **all A+AA criteria on full flows**, dated to WCAG 2.2 (2023)
W3C advises against it; some AAA is impossible for some content (§5)
test **with disabled users on their own AT**
lived-usability evidence beats the checklist — but is bounded, not ground truth (§7)
read it as a **claim**, verify the audit, still test usability
overlays don't deliver usability and can harm AT (§9)
this guide names standards, never adjudicates obligation (header, §5, §9)
operator performance/safety is HF, not interface reach (header)
